question: Suresh and Naresh can do a piece of work in 12 and 15 days, respectively. If they started working alternatively for every 1 day and if the work is started by Suresh, how many days will they take to complete 75% of the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(12, 15) = 60 units.

Target Work = 75% of 60 = 45 units.

Work done in a 2-day cycle (Suresh + Naresh) = 5 + 4 = 9 units.

Total time for 45 units = (45 ÷ 9) × 2 = 10 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Suresh = 12 days

Time taken by Naresh = 15 days

Work to be completed = 75% of the total work

**Calculations:**

⇒ Target work to be completed = 75% of 60 = 45 units

⇒ Since they work on alternate days starting with Suresh:

⇒ Work done on Day 1 (by Suresh) = 5 units

⇒ Work done on Day 2 (by Naresh) = 4 units

⇒ Work done in 1 cycle (2 days) = 5 + 4 = 9 units

⇒ Number of cycles required to complete 45 units = 45 ÷ 9 = 5 cycles

⇒ Total time taken = 5 cycles × 2 days/cycle = 10 days

**∴ The correct answer is 10 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Days Concept

When individuals work on alternate days, calculate the combined work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and determine how many cycles fit into the total work.

Work & Efficiency Relationship

Total Work = Efficiency × Time. Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken when the total work remains constant.

Pipes and Cisterns Analogy

The alternate day logic perfectly aligns with alternate hour opening of pipes in cistern problems. The underlying mathematical structure remains exactly the same.
